status: OPEN. An investigation record, not a cause. NOTE: candidate 1 was ALREADY refuted on main in reports/c96 v2 -- this file re-derived it. Only candidate 2 is new here.
rows: 19000093/51 -- segment() returns None, voiding >85% of branch mass
19000093/53 -- segments, but files Megahorn's damage in the end-of-turn slice, where the EXACT bucket rejects a legal roll difference (55 vs 53)
the_mechanism_that_IS_established: segment() (events.rs:458+) does not read move markers. It rebuilds each side's Choice, regenerates the first mover's branches, keeps those whose instruction_list is an EXACT PREFIX of the pair-generated `full`, regenerates the second mover on top of each, and requires a phase-2 branch that is also a prefix. With no eot it additionally requires list.len() == full.len(). If no (p1, p2) pair reproduces `full`, it returns None and events.rs:808-821 returns that BRANCH with zero components, marked strict:lossy_render. IT DOES NOT NECESSARILY SKIP THE BOUNDARY -- skip_lossy requires usable_branches == 0 (engine_transition_differential.py:1964-1968). Both of this report's rows are evaluated as DIVERGENT, not skipped: in sweep_i4, 19000093/51 is kind transition_diverged with branch_count 11 and 3 surviving misses (~10% of mass). An earlier revision of this file globalised c96's careful 'over 85% of the branch MASS is voided' into a false claim about the boundary.

candidate_1_REFUTED.hypothesis: the missing first-mover DecrementPP breaks the split (reports/c96 v1 named this).
candidate_1_REFUTED.refutation: segment() reads no markers at all. It prefix-matches a regeneration, so a marker absent from the engine's list is equally absent from the regeneration. Additionally the emission rule is deliberate: generate_instructions.rs:2800-2803 decrements PP only when the move is under 10 PP, and SetLastUsedMove is gated on state.use_last_used_move at :2849.
candidate_1_REFUTED.counter_evidence_from_the_rows_themselve: 19000093/51 HAS the DecrementPP and is the row that fails segmentation; 19000093/53 LACKS it and segments fine. The correlation runs backwards.
candidate_1_REFUTED.ALREADY_REFUTED_ON_MAIN: reports/c96_unattributed_source_level_causes.json, keys 19000093_51.v1s_named_candidate_is_REFUTED and 19000093_53, already carry this refutation with the same citations and the same backwards-correlation counter-evidence. C98 re-derived it. Cite c96 as the source.
candidate_1_REFUTED.mechanism_for_the_backwards_correlation: 19000093/51 is rockslide vs hydropump -- Hydro Pump has 5 PP, clears the under-10 gate and DOES emit DecrementPP, and is the row that fails segmentation. /53 is dragondance vs megahorn (20 and 10 PP), neither clears it, and it segments.

candidate_2_REFUTED.hypothesis: first_move diverges between the pair generation and the regeneration. The 16-roll gate at generate_instructions.rs:2911-2915 is `branch_on_damage && choice.first_move && pending_hp_reading_move(defender_choice)`, so if the regenerated first mover carried first_move = false its branch structure would differ from the pair generation's and no prefix could match.
candidate_2_REFUTED.refutation: checked at source and it is handled correctly. Choice::default() sets first_move: true (choices.rs:20737), build_choice's Move arm clones the move's stored Choice which carries the same default, and segment() explicitly sets second_choice.first_move = false before phase 2. The first mover is first_move = true and the second is false, which is what the pair generation does.
candidate_2_REFUTED.note: gen3/generate_instructions.rs mentions first_move at 14 sites, but only EIGHT are reads (:670, :724, :2519, :2567, :2720 rhs, :2921, :4795, :4839); one is a comment and six are writes. An earlier revision described the mention count as a read count.
candidate_2_REFUTED.the_decisive_check_this_report_did_not_s: segment() sets second_choice.first_move = false at events.rs:493, AFTER the phase-1 call at :442-450. handle_both_moves -- the pair generation -- does exactly the same at gen3/generate_instructions.rs:4920, after its phase-1 call at :4908-4916. In both, phase 1 sees a defender with first_move still true and phase 2 sees attacker false / defender true. The flags are IDENTICAL in both phases. That symmetry, not the default value alone, is what refutes the candidate.

where_to_look_next:
CORRECTED. An earlier revision ranked 'phase 2 regenerates against a state advanced by phase 1's generation' as the strongest prior. THAT IS REFUTED, by this report's own symmetry argument applied to itself: generate_instructions_from_move restores state on every exit path (gen3:2543, :2575, :2586, :2617, :2630, :2710, :2744, :2867, :2989, :3110; comment at :3115 'run_move reverses the state it applies'), AND handle_both_moves hands the same &mut State to phase 1 and every phase-2 call with no interposed apply/reverse (gen3:4908-4931), passing the phase-1 branch as `incoming` exactly as segment() does. Any residual state advance is COMMON-MODE and cancels -- the same argument that killed candidate 1.
TWO REAL DIFFERENCES between segment() and handle_both_moves, which are the live candidates:
(a) SHARED OUTPUT VECTOR AND CROSS-PHASE DEDUP. handle_both_moves pushes phase-2 results into the same state_instructions_vec it is popping phase-1 branches from with remove(0) against a pre-captured vec_len (:4918-4933), and every generate_instructions_from_move ends with combine_duplicate_instructions (:3134) which REMOVES elements (:3145). segment() uses a fresh phase2 vec and never dedups across the phase boundary.
(b) PERCENTAGE. segment() feeds phase 2 `percentage: 100.0` (events.rs:505-508) instead of the phase-1 branch's real percentage, and branch emission is gated on branch_ins.percentage != 0.0 (gen3:3117) -- so the two can produce different branch SETS.
Both are cheap to settle by instrumenting segment() to log which exit condition each candidate hits.
why_this_matters_beyond_two_rows: a segmentation failure voids a BRANCH. When it voids every branch the boundary is skipped and leaves the KPI denominator -- the hazard PR #1037 was closed for and PR #1038 documents. When it voids only some, as on both rows here, the boundary is still evaluated but on a rump branch set, which can turn a matched boundary into a divergent one. Both failure modes are live: sweep_i4 has strict:lossy_render 11 against skip:strict_all_branches_lossy 1.
